title: LandlordGuard Dwelling Fire Policy Conditions: Cancellation by the Company
content:
## A. Grounds

The company cancels a LandlordGuard Dwelling Fire Policy midterm only for:

1. nonpayment;
2. an inspection finding left uncured inside the new business period;
3. vacancy without a vacancy permit beyond the tier's vacancy cancellation period; or
4. material misrepresentation.

A notice of cancellation is copied to the mortgagee. While the notice stands the policy is pending cancellation; when the notice is rescinded it returns to in force; when the scheduled cancellation date arrives without the cure, the policy is cancelled.

## B. Nonpayment

A nonpayment notice is issued once an installment is still unpaid more than the tier's nonpayment notice period (15 calendar days on every tier) after its due date, with the cancellation scheduled the tier's nonpayment cancellation period (10 calendar days) later. The notice is rescinded only by payments received before that date totalling at least the amount due as of the notice date.

The amount due as of a date is every installment billed with a due date on or before that date, plus every fee, returned payment, additional premium and refund posted on or before it, less every payment received and return premium posted on or before it, never below 0.00.

## C. Uncured condition — the new business period

An underwriting cancellation notice for an uncured condition is issued only within the new business period that starts on the original effective date. The period is counted in calendar days with the original effective date as day 1, so the last day to issue the notice is the original effective date plus the tier's new business period days (60 on every tier) minus 1. The original effective date is taken from the policy record.

| Hypothetical original effective date | Day 60 (last day to issue) | Notice issued on day 60 | Notice issued on day 61 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 March | 29 April | within the period | outside the period |

## D. Vacancy without a permit — the vacancy period

A vacancy cancellation notice is issued only after the vacancy period that starts on the vacancy start date. The vacancy period is counted with the vacancy start date as day 1, so the notice may be issued once the days vacant exceed the tier's vacancy cancellation period. The days vacant are the consecutive calendar days the building has been vacant up to the notice date, counting the vacancy start date as day 1 and leaving out days inside a vacancy permit. The vacancy start date and the permit dates are taken from the policy record.

| Hypothetical case (tier period 90 days, vacancy start 1 June, no permit) | Days vacant | Notice may be issued |
|---|---|---|
| Notice date 29 August | 90 | no — 90 does not exceed 90 |
| Notice date 30 August | 91 | yes |

## E. Scheduling and rescission of underwriting and vacancy notices

An underwriting or vacancy notice schedules the cancellation the tier's underwriting cancellation period (30 calendar days) after the notice date, and never sooner than the mortgagee notice period (10 calendar days) when a mortgagee is on file. A vacancy notice is rescinded when a tenant moves in or a vacancy permit is issued before that date, and an uncured-condition notice when the condition is cured before that date.

## F. Return premium on a cancellation by the company

A cancellation by the company credits pro rata, with no retention and no minimum earned premium.
